_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: Tourist Season, 2007 · the map
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 27, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Two days after: the tourist asks where the walk goes — the alley, the road, the post, the stairs, the log — and Wood, instead of answering, draws it on a napkin, and then keeps the napkin. It goes on the corkboard a month later as the walk map. This is where it comes from. Panel 1: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a tourist on a seawall bench pointing at an open town map beside a thin man and a small dog (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 2: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man drawing on a paper napkin with a pen on a bench (in this panel: WOOD). Panel 3: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close on a paper napkin with a hand-drawn dotted route past a few small landmarks and a date in the corner. Panel 4: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man tucking a napkin into his own coat pocket while a tourist's hand stays held out (in this panel: WOOD). No text, no lettering, no speech balloons, no signature; leave clean space in each panel where balloons would go. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_main_street shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31; @loc_main_street for the setting.
